questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes supervised learning from unsupervised learning?

choices.text: Supervised learning trains on labeled data, while unsupervised learning finds patterns without labels.
choices.response: Correct. Supervised learning uses labeled ground truth; unsupervised learning discovers structure without labels.

choices.text: Supervised learning only works on small datasets, while unsupervised learning only works on large datasets.
choices.response: Incorrect. Both can scale; the key difference here is the presence of labels.

choices.text: Supervised learning only works on structured data, while unsupervised learning only works on unstructured data.
choices.response: Incorrect. Supervision is about labels, not whether data is structured.

choices.text: Supervised learning is deep learning, while unsupervised learning is classical machine learning.
choices.response: Incorrect. Deep learning can be supervised or unsupervised; it is not the separator.

questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labeled ground truth; unsupervised learning discovers structure without labels.
